collections.title: Ancient and Medieval World · Main Survey
collections.summary: Ten comparative lectures follow broad historical periods from early urban societies to around 1500. Regional and evidence studies are separate choices, with their own chronologies.

chapters.title: Late antiquity and the first Muslim polities
Later medieval worlds and the threshold of 1500

collections.title: Ancient and Medieval World · Regional and Evidence Studies
collections.summary: Choose a region or historical problem. Each branch has an explicit scope; early livelihood histories and later memory studies keep their own dates rather than inheriting the date of a nearby survey ID.

collections.title: Iran, Mesopotamia, and Central Asia
collections.summary: Households, contracts, mobile power, towns, and manuscript communities across distinct ancient and medieval periods.

collections.title: Mediterranean and European documentary worlds
collections.summary: Compare inscriptions, citizenship, charters, and medieval land records; this is not one continuous legal tradition.

collections.title: Red Sea, Nile, and Ethiopian histories
collections.summary: Water, property, religious institutions, and household documents from ancient Saba and Kush to medieval communities.

collections.title: Books, translation, and material knowledge
collections.summary: A comparative study of Baghdad, Dunhuang, Goryeo, and Timbuktu, with explicit dates and evidence limits.

collections.title: China, Korea, and Japan
collections.summary: Written states, household records, estates, and courtly writing; the examples move among different periods.

collections.title: South Asian fields, institutions, and poetry
collections.summary: Reservoirs, donors, assemblies, monastic grants, and poetic evidence across South Asia.

collections.title: Southeast Asian landscapes and maritime institutions
collections.summary: Mainland settlements and sacred landscapes, Java and Bali, then comparative port documents around the Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia.

collections.title: Eastern and Central African interiors
collections.summary: Early livelihoods, fields and furnaces, settlement, exchange, and later political memory. These are separate timelines, not a medieval Swahili sequence.

collections.title: Swahili coasts and western Indian Ocean islands
collections.summary: Early ports and hinterlands, island settlement, coins, and coastal household life.

collections.title: Sahelian towns and Nigerian metalwork
collections.summary: Archaeological studies of settlement, trade, craft, and authority across distinct West African regions.

collections.title: Comparing African state formation
collections.summary: A comparative lecture on Lake Chad, Mapungubwe, and Kongo, rather than a single regional succession.

collections.title: Mesoamerican neighborhoods, states, and records
collections.summary: Classic urban and Maya evidence followed by highland households, painted histories, and explicitly colonial land records.

collections.title: Andean societies and knowledge
collections.summary: Earlier states, household obligations, and knotted-cord records in a longer Andean history.

collections.title: Indigenous North American landscapes and communities
collections.summary: Arid landscapes, eastern towns and seasonal worlds, Plains and Arctic homes, then Pacific coast and river management.

collections.title: Caribbean societies before 1492
collections.summary: A complete short regional orientation, retained as a focused exception rather than joined to an unrelated mainland history.

collections.title: Oceanic settlement and inhabited landscapes
collections.summary: Remote Oceanic settlement and maritime centers, followed by distinct landscape histories in Australia, Rapa Nui, Aotearoa, and Hawaiʻi.
